# Testing standards

Apply these when writing or changing tests or test documents. The project's existing test style wins: match
the framework, folder layout, naming and helpers already used. The framework rules in
`.claude/rules/testing/` add the details for each tool.

## Good tests

- One behaviour per test, named after the expected behaviour ("rejects an expired token"), arranged as
  set up → act → check.
- Independent: no test relies on another test's data or run order. Each creates the data it needs and cleans
  up after itself.
- Deterministic: no fixed sleeps; wait for a condition (element visible, response received, job finished).
  Control time, randomness and external services with the project's mocking or fake tools.
- Meaningful checks: assert the outcome that matters (values, state, messages), not just "no error".
- Stable UI locators: prefer accessible roles and labels or dedicated test IDs (`data-testid`, `data-cy`,
  accessibility identifiers) over CSS classes, text that changes, or long XPath.
- Tag or name every automated test with its test case ID (e.g. `TC-US-012-03`) so results trace back.

## Never

- Weaken, skip or delete a test just to make a run pass. If a test is wrong, say why and fix it openly.
- Use real customer or personal data, or production credentials. Use generated data and test accounts.
- Hard-code environment URLs or secrets; read them from configuration.
- Run load, security or destructive tests against shared or production environments without explicit
  permission.

## When a test fails

Decide which it is before acting: a product bug (raise it with `/bug-report`), a test problem (fix the test),
an environment or data problem (report it), or a flaky test (re-run once; if it passes, record it as flaky and
find the cause).
